prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 多级表头 · 半年度指标 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "指标" spans 1 col × 2 row; "2023 年" spans 2 col × 1 row; "2024 年" spans 2 col × 1 row; "备注" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "指标" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 107px
  col 2: header "2023 年 › 上半年" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "2023 年 › 下半年" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "2024 年 › 上半年" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 5: header "2024 年 › 下半年" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 40px
  col 6: header "备注" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 303px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 516px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 515px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"四个半年列整齐，表头完整；但备注列偏窄，首条备注占三行，且“百分点”被拆开，行标题也换行。"},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"半年列均衡，首条备注只占两行，整体紧凑；但“汇率”跨行，较长的行标题也换行。"},"C":{"grade":"bad","why":"数值列占据过多宽度，备注列被挤得很窄，文字多次断行，导致行高失衡且难以阅读。"},"D":{"grade":"poor","why":"备注列较宽，但四个半年表头都把“年”挤到下一行，削弱了分组表头的清晰度。"},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"四个半年列均衡且表头完整，备注分两行并保持“汇率”和“百分点”完整；行标题虽换行，但各行仍易于横向比较。"},"F":{"grade":"good","why":"行标题保持单行，半年列清晰；但首条备注占三行，且“增量”跨行，首行显得较高。"}},"best":["E"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"B、E 的差别较细微，判断主要取决于首条备注的换行位置。"}
